tei:titleStmt.tei:title: Prayer of the Guest Chaplain of the U.S. Senate: Rabbi Gustav N. Hausmann on 12 December 1918

tei:div.tei:head: Prayer of the Guest Chaplain of the U.S. Senate: Rabbi Gustav N. Hausmann on 12 December 1918

tei:lg.tei:l: Merciful God and Heavenly Father,
Thou who didst grant unto us the privilege
of being victorious on the side of right against might;
Thou who didst choose America
to enlighten the nations of the earth;
Thou who didst endow us
with the gift and spirit of democracy,
we beseech Thee to continue to guide and lead us.
Make us worthy of these blessings.
May our victories, triumphs, and successes
not make us arrogant and haughty.
May it not be said of this new-chosen Nation
what was said of the ancient-chosen people:
“But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked * * *
then he forsook the God which made him,
and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation.” (Deuteronomy 32:15)
Bless, O God, this great Republic
with abundance and honor,
with peace and good will.
We especially beseech Thee
to bless, shield, and protect
the President of the United States,
the crusader of modern democracy.
Bless the Congress of the United States of America,
that it may truly exemplify democracy, equality, and justice.
May the deliberations at the peace conference abroad
result for the great benefit of humanity
and redound to the honor of this Nation.
May Thy name thus be glorified in and through us.
Amen.

tei:note.tei:p: A reference to the early planning for the Paris Peace Conference (1919-1920). President Woodrow Wilsom left the United States for France on 13 December 1918.
